test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 28 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Why is air transport less popular for freight movement in India?

options.text: It is widely available in rural and remote villages.
It requires minimal infrastructure for operation.
It is expensive and ideal only for light, high-value goods.
It is slower and less efficient than water transport

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is expensive and ideal only for light, high-value goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **High Cost of Air Transport:** Air transport is significantly more expensive compared to other modes of freight transport, such as road, rail, or water. This high cost limits its use primarily to light and high-value goods like electronics, jewelry, and pharmaceuticals.
 
• **Suitability for Specific Goods:** Due to its cost, air freight is ideal for goods that are time-sensitive or perishable, such as flowers or medical supplies. This makes it unsuitable for bulkier, low-value commodities such as agricultural produce or construction materials.
 
• **Limited Accessibility:** Air transport infrastructure is concentrated in urban and metropolitan areas. Rural and remote regions in India lack the necessary airport facilities, making it an impractical option for freight movement in such areas.
 
• **Infrastructure Requirements:** Unlike other modes of transport, air transport requires complex and expensive infrastructure, such as airports, air traffic control systems, and advanced security measures, which further increases its operational costs.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** Air transport contributes significantly to carbon emissions, making it less environmentally friendly compared to other modes of transportation. This further restricts its widespread adoption for freight movement in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparison with Other Modes of Transport:**

 
 
• **Road Transport:** Road transport is widely used for freight movement in India due to its extensive network and ability to provide last-mile connectivity. It is cost-effective for short and medium distances.
 
• **Rail Transport:** Railways are cost-efficient for transporting heavy and bulk goods over long distances. India’s rail network is one of the largest in the world, making it a preferred mode for industries.
 
• **Water Transport:** Waterways are the cheapest mode of transport for bulk commodities. However, their usage in India is limited to specific routes like the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers and coastal shipping.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Goods Transported by Air:**
 
 
• High-value goods such as **gold, diamonds, and other precious metals**.
 
• Perishable commodities like **fruits, vegetables, seafood, and flowers**.
 
• Time-sensitive products such as **pharmaceuticals and organs for transplant**.
 
• Electronics and luxury items like **smartphones, laptops, and branded accessories**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Expanding Air Freight in India:**
 
 
• **Lack of Infrastructure:** Many regions lack airports or cargo handling facilities, limiting the reach of air freight services.
 
• **High Operational Costs:** The cost of fuel, maintenance, and skilled manpower increases the overall expense of air transport.
 
• **Regulatory Hurdles:** Complex customs and regulatory procedures can delay air freight operations.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **UDAN (Ude Desh Ka Aam Naagrik)** scheme aims to improve regional air connectivity and make air travel affordable for the masses.
 
• Development of **dedicated freight corridors** and modernization of airports to handle cargo efficiently.
 
• Incentives for using environmentally friendly aircraft and technologies to reduce the carbon footprint of air transport.
